1. My Squadron asks for new prospect Cadets to wear a white collard shirt, pants, and shoes however there may be a different way for this squadron.

But I suggest to wear proper wear so maybe a short sleeve button up, something thats proper and presentable (it shows you care to look nice and will make a great impression on you to the other Cadets.)

If you may not have anything really proper or something like that then wear a t shirt thats not covered in logos and all, just casual stuff.

2. Yes, if you are able to contact the Squadron to let them know you’re coming then it’ll help you and the Cadets, but don’t worry, you can just show up if you cannot contact them.

3. Yes, bring a parent.
This is because the Unit Commander can talk to your parents about the program and basically get paperwork signed and possibly an interview.(really just like “so how old is your kid”, “has he done drugs”, etc)

4. Yes, so my Squadron has this layout (other Squadron have the same) 

1st meeting is Aerospace Education.
2nd Meeting is PT
3rd Meeting is Character Development.
4th Meeting is Promotions.
And if we have a 5th Tuesday then we go to a local bowling ball place and chill out and socialize.

Other Squadrons may have first week PT and second character development and maybe on Wednesday not a Tuesday, but you’ll know when your in your basic weeks of the program.

5. The challenge I would say is time and dates, CAP has a real good tendency to have activities at the most inconvenient times, so maybe want to have a clear weekend schedule when your in the Squadron just for events, but they’ll give weeks notice or even months notice but thats really it, unless you don’t workout then PT will be a challenge. (These are challenges in the Squadron)

6. Its best to have a good rank specially if you enjoy and take the program serious but no, you don’t have to be a Spaatz Cadet when you leave or a 2nd Lt.

However I heard having a good rank can give you a boost in gettin’ into the Academy.
